review: I am an older woman and I am a casual gamer.  My son taught me gaming on the PC. I have tried a few other farming games on steam. This one I like the best. I am not into multiplayer games.  I love how relaxing this game  is for me after a stressful day. I love farming,  landscaping, and interior designing.  I love doing it alone.  The keyboard and the mouse are much better then the gaming controller.  I would recommend it to anyone wanting to play a farming game solo.

After playing Farm Together for almost 3,300 hours, I can officially say that its my all time favourite game ever!

You can zone out, listen to some music in the background and just play play play.

There's so much to do and it fits many different play styles. If you like making things look pretty and aesthetically pleasing then this is the game for you. If you like grinding and spending lots of time working towards a fun achievable and rewarding goal then this is the game for you. If you like making lots of money and doing some fun calculations to see what crop, tree, fish animal and flowers get you the most money, then this is also the game for you.

The dev team releases VERY frequent updates and actually listens to what the community wants, bug fixes within hours of the community telling them about said bugs, and they also release fun super cheep dlc packs with LOTS of content while also making sure that dlc is mostly for aesthetics rather than any kind of pay to win content.

The art style for the game is simplistic, colourful and friendly. The interface and options menu has lots of neat features.

The game doesn't have any set storyline or any finish, but instead lets you chose how you play, what you do and allows for almost endless possibilities!

You start out you game with just a few thousand dollars, some fish, crops, trees and flowers, where you go from there is your choice. You can decide to follow quests which earn you ribbons to spend on things like gas stations to fuel a customizable tractor, buildings to speed things up and make life on you farm easier, sprinklers to water crops which will lower the time to take before harvesting them or flowers to earn more money off them.

And if you ever get bored of your current farm setup and want to start over but don't want to take the time to make all of you money back then they have an answer for that too! You can recycle your entire farm and start from the beginning while still keeping all of your hard earned money, ribbons, diamonds, tickets, houses and special buildings!

I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a peaceful, calming and fun gaming experience where you can literally play for hours alone or with friends!

Edit: for people commenting on this review. I am unable to reply to comments, but if you would like me to reply to a comment then please feel free to add me or comment on my profile and i'll happily reply to any comments you have about my review.

Edit #2: I would also like to point out, yes, I obviously haven't been actively playing all of my almost 4k hours in game. Many of those hours have been afk over night and a rough estimate of my actual play time would still be approximately 1.5-2k hours.

I loved this game SO much. I often left it running idle (hence my >3000 hours logged, yikes) so that I could check in to find crops already grown, eggs already laid by chickens, etc. I played alone, I played with my boyfriend, I played with strangers. Its screenshots became my laptop backgrounds and my calendar pages. Its music became the soundtrack of my life for a year. This game was wonderful. Thank you devs! :)

If you are not sure if you should buy this game (which is most likely the reason you look at the reviews) then let me help you with this.

- First of all, it is definitly NOT comparable with games like Stardew Valley, since this game focusses purely on the farming aspect and has no "side stories" or RPG-elements. The game plays more like a mobile farming game, which sounds negative but in this case but it's definitly not.

- The focus on the game is building up a farm, which is oddly addictive. You have two levels, the player level (unlocks customizations for your character, emotes and your tractor) and your farm level, which unlocks new buildings, animals, plants and decorations. 
This motivates you to keep playing, since the more progress you make, the more content you unlock. It's a circle of "Oh I cant wait what I get on the next level!" that keeps the game motivating.

- It's VERY important for me to point out that EVERY aspect in this game is unlockable with game progress, there is NO Paywall or even an option to buy "ingame currency". I am pointing that out since I've read Reviews stating otherwise, complaining about "Diamonds you have to buy with money". This is wrong.
You get Money buy harvesting plants and animal products, Diamonds by selling your goods at market stands and later in the game pink "ribbons", which you get by selling "higher" products like Jam.

- This game is not a "simulator", it has a cute comic look and everything is peaceful and friendly. 
pigs give truffels, rabbits give carrots and cows give milk, so there is no "slaughtering"  in the game. 
Only fishes are actually caught, guess being friendly doesnt include fishes. (poor guys.)
Therefore don't buy this if you look for an economy/farming simulator, if the preview videos did not make that clear already.

- A big part of this game (in my opinion) is the multiplayer. (It's called farm together for a reason.) You can join other servers (the owner can always decide how many rights certain visitors have, so don't worry about some random dude reconstructing your farm) and you can play together with friends. The farm has a "money pool", so whatever your friend harvests, plants or builds it's coming from the farm money, which makes playing together rewarding for every player. 
So if you like playing together with your friends and enjoy a peaceful session of farming and building up a farm together then this game is for you. 

To put everything together in one short summary:

The game is incredibly addictive. No matter if its feeding animals, harvesting or watering plants, expanding your farm or decorating the area you already have, there is always something to do. You think "okay, I am done for now" and then, before you manage to close the game you see something that you forgot. Especially with friends this game is a very catching experience.

The developers really put love in this game with cute and adorable animations and a lot of new updates. 
The game is still in early access, so dont expect a finished game (and dont judge the game by that) but it already offers a very playable amount of content. 

I can definitly recommend this game, especially for the relatively low price. 
If you are looking for a new stardew valley or a game like Staxel then you should continue your search, since this game does not offer RPG elements (yet) nor does it allow you to terraform the environment.
But you like farming games and you always wanted to build up a "comic style" farm together with friends, then this is the game for you.

The game so far has been delightful to play. It's been on my "Follow" list for a long time. I'm very guilty of being drawn to cute looking games.
I have non-epileptic seizures frequently. Finding games that are not stress inducing in any way shape or form are pure win for me. I cannot have any kind of adrenaline running or i run the risk of seizures. Stress magnifies my chances of having seizures hundredfold, so to find games that just are designed, like this one to chill you out, relax you and give you peace are amazing.
For the first while i was just running around plowing the land and planting crops. Watering them and harvesting them. Admittedly they didn't tell you that you needed a vegetable stand to SELL your crops. You have to kind of use your brain some times i think. That can be difficult. More often than not i'm left in a semi comatosed state for a good week or so after a seizure.. My brain simply doesn't work. I'm just coming off the back off a seizure now just over a week ago and maybe my confusion is due to that. 
When you get your tractor! Epic! From plowing 1 tile at a time to 9.. I just drove around plowing ALL the tiles! :D

I'm easily entertained. I like cute, appealing to the eye graphics. The colour pallette is simply beautiful and very easy to look at which is important for me because i have migraines A LOT of the time. 
I am only just discovering animals, fish and flowers. I thought i'd hop out the game, get a drink and leave a review. It's a beautiful game and very relaxing. I think that was the word i was looking for. Relaxing. Not many games can let you sit, relax and play. Just to play it and enjoy it. 
Have fun folks!

Oh yes. On edit. I meant to mention that i get injured a lot of the time from my seizures. You'd be very surprised, or at least i was by how many games on steam simply do not have controller support, even partially. This game has full controller support. I've been using one because my elbows are a mess due to the seizures and it works brilliantly. No idea how the keyboard and mouse works.

Heh. Second edit:
Well I've gotten into the game a lot more now. Clocked up quite a few hours!
Literally the day after writing this review, i went into multiple seizures. I think we stopped counting at 9. This game was what i was playing when i went into them. I slept for a while when they eventually stopped hours later.. Game still running (LOL!). I am pretty dense for a good long while after my seizures.
This time i was again left unable to comprehend words, no matter how simple. A good 70% of things said to me were unable to be understood. I couldn't understand things on the farm. But i was able to hop into other peoples farms and play. Because you're helping people they don't mind you plowing, harvesting ect. I couldn't really function enough to do anything on my own and spent most of my time over the last week playing on other people's farms. So even if you're not wanting to do the stuff yourself you can just "find farms" on the main menu and potter around on other people's places which gives you the experience of the game play.
You also learn things by visiting other people and get ideas on how to make your farm look nice without all the trial and error they have no doubt gone through :)

Ehhhh, I really want to like this game, but if you're looking similar to Stardew Valley you might (will) be disappointed. 

I am recommending this game because I still kinda have fun, and I can appreciate the effort that was put into the game, but it wasn't what I was looking for and let me tell you why before you make this purchase looking for a Stardew Valley-like game.

The farming aspect is done very well, art style, animations are well done. Hundreds of stuff to buy and grow on your farm. My biggest grip however is the *UNSKIPPABLE TIME GATE* on everything. 

In Stardew Valley, when you are done planting and watering your crops, you have 2 choices: either you skip time by going to sleep, or you do other activities such as social/mining/monster hunting/fishing, you never feel restricted by crops growing time.

In Farm Together, everything is gated behind REAL TIME with no skip (yes watering crops SLIGHTLY lowers the time, but still 100% hinders gameplay). Fishing takes time, growing crops takes time, animal products take time, meaning that your gameplay sessions are very LIMITED, you can't grind this game like you can Stardew Valley, realistically, you log in, you gather your stuff, plant and water your stuff, then log off. For example, I just planted Watermelons which take 2 days (48 hours), to grow, if you water them, it takes them 1 day 17 hours to grow.

Once you've invested your money in all your farm stuff you're left with 2 options really: 1- gather wells for 25g each (which you can't even loot with your tractor, so you gotta loot them 1 by 1) 2- go for low time crops/animals/fishes with terrible profit returns.

Seems to me like there is enough content in the game to let the player skip time (at least skip seasons, which is 17 minutes in real time)

Their design philosophy as is, is no different than any farming sim you can find on mobile, gating you behind time and restricting your game sessions to 1-2 hours while not giving you other meaningful side activities to do while you wait.

So if you don't mind having your gameplay sessions restricted by time gates, I'd say this is a fantastic game, but if you're looking to hardcore grind a farming sim like you would Stardew Valley, you might find yourself disappointed, just like I was.

Be aware this game has the mobile game vibe with planting and waiting for x hours in realtime mechanic.
It might be fun in the first few hours but gets annoying real quick and you might find yourself exhausted rather than relaxed. Also there is no planting, growing and farming mechanic. You have a tractor you click on 9 tiles and tractor jumps and digs/farms/plants/irrigates with same animation. So imagine doing this for basically everything. I would highly suggest watching 2-3 hours of video first. If you can bear watching samething for 3 hours. Then you can buy the game.

With over 515 hours in the game at this point, I'd have to be INSANE to not recommend this game. For me, it's the most fun farming game that I've ever played. Is it realistic farming? Nope! But that's one of the reasons that I love it. There's a huge fantasy element to it that makes it cute and charming, while leaving lots of room for personal customization. Even after several years of playing, I continue to visit my farm and make changes. And I'll continue to do so.  There IS one thing that, to a few of us, becomes annoying - when you plant stuff, the tractor JUMPS up and down like a dang bucking bronco. That gets old after a while. Other than that, I really enjoy the mechanics of the game. You also get to have a pet, and there are a variety of them. How can you go wrong with a cute pet following you around?

So yes, I highly recommend Farm Together to anyone that wants to farm, but in a cute way.

This is a fun cute little game to play with friends or a spouse, HOWEVER it has a system where obviously your crops or anything else needs to grow for a set amount of time and watering can reduce that time slightly. This makes the game feel like a mobile game, you log on to harvest, replant, get off and get on the next day. That as the core gameplay doesn't have me coming back anymore. If there were a mechanic where you could say like sleep in the bed of your house to progress time one real life day every season change or something that would actually keep me playing and not treat it like clock work the game would have me playing still. Even if the time reduced to harvest was reduced that would help this game, otherwise its a really nice game.

The wife and I enjoy playing this game for casual downtime. You can play solo, friends only, or open multiplayer if you wish. There are time-limited events but there are so many multiplayer farms open to the public they are easy to complete. You can easily lose track of time as you design your farms, your houses, rearrange layouts, etc. Really fun game!

I don't do reviews often but this little gem is exactly what I look for in games. Relaxing turn your brain off and just chillout gameplay. If I had to give a short review i'd say it's like a 3D hayday but without all the MT rubbish. Not ony that but it has tons of crops and things to do. 

The first few hours you might think OMG timers i don't want to wait but as your farm grows you are so busy with so many different things they are hardly an issue and let's face it, crop take time to grow, if they was instant where would be the gameplay. 

I don't want to spoil the progression for those who have not expereinced it but let's just say that you need to keep farming and building up your money for later content :)

I had fun with this game playing with my 8-year-old son. We built a farm with a rather chaotic layout based on whatever crops and animals we were asked to produce at any given time. He looked forward to unlocking new animals, and he especially enjoyed the new looks for his farmer and pet every few levels. After about 33 hours, the fun wore off a bit and he moved on to other things. Now, 33 hours might not sound like a whole lot, but its a complete bargain when compared to hiring a babysitter or most other forms of child entertainment. 

Meanwhile, I went back to the drawing board and built a better farm layed out in a more systematic way. It became more of an engineering project, moving onto workers and optimization of their layout and routines. This phase lasted about another 50-70 hours of playing time (much of it afk) before I switched to finishing off achievements and it was a bit more of a grind. In the end the game fizzled out a bit, with the last achievement coming down to pressing combinations of "x" and mouse clicks a few thousand times while watching sports on TV. 

Was it fun? Yes, but the time to stop is when you first notice that its becoming a chore. Those first few hours were great, and it really helps to have someone to play with.

My girlfriend and I were looking for a game for this sole purpose. To Farm Together!

While the general gameplay feels rewarding and fun, the game seems to be losing momentum with us. However, I feel that the developers Could enhance this game a bit more to motivate us to continue to play. The biggest problem with this game is not the game mechanics, those are fun. The problem is that we don't feel a sense of accomplishment. ---After raising more and more crops, you unlock additional properties to farm, but we don't feel connected to the experience because WHAT HAPPENS when you are making hundreds of thousands each harvest? Do you take that money and improve upon a nice beautiful homestead? where you can upgrade your farm home? No. Is there a mechanic for doing something, ANYTHING other than buying more seeds, not really. Despite some cute aesthetic props you can purchase and plop down, there isn't any reaally rewarding feeling you get from harvesting. Other than buying more expensive seeds and re-planting. There is no overall objective. I just don't understand. am I just to continue buying more expensive crops, for the sake of planting more expensive crops?

I really wish I could visit other players farms. Or literally have some sort of NPC town that we could buy stuff in. Do the paved roads and paths do anything beyond aesthetics? No. It would have been cool to see a very minor movement increase while walking on paved surfaces.

But more importantly, We don't get why we should continue to plant crops. Is it to earn money? and to do what with? repeat with a differernt crop?

There is no Rent to pay, there is no homestead building and upgrading. There is no farm pet, like a dog. I kinda wished this game had more Sims like qualities to it.

EDIT: to those suggesting we might start a Real garden, we do! Our home is full of plants and I do gardening regularly myself!

As you've noticed, I have over 400 hours in this game alone. You do not NEED the DLC to play the game, it's an enhancement to an already nice looking and relaxing game. It adds cosmetic things for your farm and home, and some new crops.

It's a simple farm game where you can grow crops, flowers, trees, feed your animals and fish. It's nothing difficult, but it is pleasing graphically to the eye and the music is SUPER relaxing. I've had a ton fun just decorating, messing around and using the game as an overall relaxer, the only real time limit to the game is the events that are hosted; but none I've come across are too hard, unless you are one that isn't as active.

I have seen people liken the game to a similar Farmville vibe without energy. The only waiting is grow timers, which could be a deal breaker for some, but if you are familiar with the series then it's no big deal and comes with the territory. There are no destructive events, no monsters, everything in the game is super chill.

Are you looking for some mindless entertainment and relaxation?  Then this could be for you.  Farm Together does not really present a challenge, defined goal, or any specific obstacle to overcome.  You just build a farm a your own leisurely pace.  Crops don't wither if you don't harvest them, nor do flowers, and your animals don't care if you neglect them.  You always make money harvesting, and your farm will always continue  to expand as you play.  You can do as much as you want to do.  Oh, and helping others grants you an experience boost to the XP and money you make on your own farm for a period of time. The only frustration I see is the time limits it takes to grow some crops.  At any rate, sit back, relax, and watch the fields grow.

An ultra-casual agriculture sim-lite that styled after the massively popular Farmville. Depending on your play style there's a lot of fun to be found in this little game. 
It's a very chill game. You're never locked out of anything that waiting 15 or so minutes can't fix. There are no picky townspeople to satisfy. In fact, there are no townspeople at all. It's just you, your real life friends (or internet strangers) and the trappings of subsidized farming. And, depending on what kind of person you are it can either be a really good time or an absolute candy-coated slogfest. 
Leveling your farm and upgrading the produce provides a very fun, yet fleeting challenge. In the beginning you'll find yourself doing a lot of hurrying up to wait. Then after that you'll be doing a lot of harvesting and replanting. Then, once you get some hired help and a beefy farm you'll be doing a whole lot of jack shit while the game idles in the background making your computer fan heat the whole room up. This is the progression of Farm Together. 
If you're the kind of player who tanks games and racks up 50+ hour playtimes in a week, then Farm Together might hold your interest for a month or so. Tops. Provided, you really have to like farm sims. If not, don't bother. It also helps to play with another person, as harvesting thousands of crops gets old really fucking fast and the only farming the greater Farm Together community seems interested in is the farming for XP on the mega farms overloaded with so many assets that it makes my gaming PC chug. 
Resource creep is mitigated by buildings such as the warehouse and shops. Throughout my entire play time none of my resources ever became trivial. Something always needed something else so there was always a smooth resource-in-currency-out. Now, if only the game provided some sort of automation to help things go even smoother. 
If farm sims are your wheelhouse, then you may find this game addictive. Many a time I've stopped in, only for 'a few minutes' to turn into an hour or so. It's like a domino effect. As soon as you've finished planting one thing, another thing across the map is ready for harvesting, or a quest finishes, or some other task comes along to drag you back in. It's fun at first, but like most other features of this game it turns into a chore. Earlier this week, I popped in to Sweet Potato Acres for the first time in a few days and quickly got to work. Halfway through collecting a harvest of 420 artichokes, I stopped and asked myself:

"Why am I doing this?"

Then I closed the game. 
This wasn't just a moment of video game-induced existentialism. At that point I honestly could not answer why I was bothering with Farm Together. All of the crops had been unlocked, as well as most everything else. My farm had been recycled. All I had to look forward to was the endless cycle of quests, which gave me medals. Medals I'd have no choice but to hoard as I already had all the buildings. So then those coveted little trinkets become useless too. There was no real reward.

The Search for Farm screen may as well be a leaderboard. Once you break into the millions gold and diamonds become point scores instead of currency. They're rendered completely useless, as because no matter how many crops you put down, flowers you grow or animals you raise you'll still have more of it than you could ever know what to do with. Then all satisfaction that could be had has been robbed from you. Game over. Go play something else. 

All in all, this was a fun way to pass about 100 or so hours with my best friend. After that it's just depressing. 

PROS and CONS

[Overall] 
+ Cute, colorful aesthetic.
+ Charming, relaxing soundtrack.
+ The farming is decently robust for such a straightforward game.
+ The early game gives you a lot to look foward to.
+ Nothing of consequence is locked behind a paywall. The DLCs are mostly cosmetic, with the contained crops being more decorative than giving you any sort of gameplay advantage.*
+ Crops, animals, flowers, etc, all produce in slightly different ways, which is neat I guess.
+ The game is fairly accomodating to those with different levels of time investment.

* I've heard some say that the real value in DLC are the houses, which allow you to farm more tickets. I'm iffy on this, as I ended up with more than enough tickets with the base game homes alone. YMMV. 

-The community, while helpful and extremely polite, only seems interested in XP and event farming. Not that I blame them. There really isn't much else to do.
- Farming quickly becomes repetitive and overwhelming.
- No landscaping = having to design your farm around landmarks you may or may not want.
- Some of the DLCs are kind of skinny for the price, even if it is just a few dollars (USD).

[Events]
+ Fun, silly seasonal event crops are a cute change of pace to the usual offerings.
+ They happen pretty regularly so there's always one on the horizon.
+ Unlocking the event items gives you something to do.

- Events are so short that if you don't have time to devote to the game you can't unlock all the items.
- ...Unless you go to one of those bot-run mega farms.
- ...But only if you get their soon enough, as everyone else is there too. 
- They too, get boring after a while.


[Homes]

+ A cute way to decorate your farm.
+ The primary way of farming tickets.
+ The DLC offers lots of cool options.

- If you're not into interior decoration these are effectively ticket farms.
- Some of the house interiors have weird layouts and room sizes.

If you still need something to scratch that exploration/farming/light life sim itch, here are some suggestions:

Animal Crossing New Horizons - The Best AC game yet, don't let anyone tell you otherwise. WARNING: As of the time of this review it's is basically a AAA early access game. Stardew Valley - Everyone keeps yammering about it for a reason. The best of the genre, even with it's faults. A tough act to follow as far as PC farm/life sims go and unbeatable for the price. It's a really good time, I promise. 

Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town -  A remake of the 17-year-old Harvest Moon: Friends of Mineral Town for the GBA and a classic in the franchise. THIS REVIEW IS MY OWN UNBIASED OPINION - I was not compensated or rewarded for this review in any way.

I bought this game on a whim - and I ended up enjoying it a lot.

[u][b]BUYER NOTICE:[/b][/u]  Do NOT expect this game to be Stardew Valley/Harvest Moon/My Time at Portia.  It is not.  This game focuses on solely the farming aspect, there are no other characters (other than in multiplayer), there's no combat, there's no relationships (unless you get REALLY attached to your animals).  What this game IS: a relaxing, casual farming experience to play by yourself or with friends whenever you have time.

This game lets you farm plants and animals in real-time, with each season lasting 17 minutes.  The real-time aspect is similar to mobile farming games, however there are absolutely no microtransactions, and you can cut down significantly on growth times by watering the plants when they need it.  Anyways, each time you harvest a plant/animal, you earn coins (buy more plants/animals with this), and a produce item (eggs, vegetables, etc.) which can either be traded at a market stand for gems (used to buy structures) or used at another structure to make it into something else (I think?  I'm not that far yet).  Rinse and repeat, unlocking new plants, animals, structures, and decorations as you level up your farm.

Time progresses even when you're not playing, so your plants can mature and your animals will produce if they have enough food, but the nice thing is plants don't wilt or anything, so you can take as much time as you need between logins.  In other words, you can log off and not worry about your plants or animals dying or something silly.

Early game is quite repetitive until you get your tractor, so earn as much XP as you can.  Farming becomes much more enjoyable and fast once you have the tractor.  There are also a fair amount of character customization; you can change your tractor, your clothes, your hair, your gender, etc.

All in all, the game is REALLY relaxing.  The music is soft and fitting, the gameplay is easy and straight-forward, and the game runs smooth even with maxxed graphics, I'm fairly sure older machines could run this game just fine.  The game has a nice ambience to it as well, each season has its own color palettes and effects like snow.

[b]SUGGESTIONS TO THE DEVS:[/b]

[list]
[*]Ambient critters that run around your farm would be cute (besides butterflies), maybe squirrels or birds and such.
[*]Moar upgrades and structures!
[*]In line with more upgrades, maybe a tool to make animal harvesting easier (I couldnt find a way to use the tractor)?
[*]A way to quickly move large parts of your farm would be good; something like it puts you in a birds eye view mode and you click to pick up and click to move instantly, so when you're shifting your tree farm around it doesnt take 3 years of running back and forth.
[*]PLEASE PLEASE get rid of whatever it is that makes the edges of the screen / grass blurry.  I've tried turning Ambient Occlusion and Depth of Field on/off/every which way and it never goes away.  It's literally terrible and hurts my eyes.  I dont care if it hits gfx performance to turn it off, at least give us the option.  If I look anywhere other than the middle of my screen it burns my eyes :(
[*]Early game could be a bit less grindy, it might turn people away from the game before they even get their tractor.  Maybe just a bit less XP for early levels?
[/list]

After I started having some money I was able to play a bit more, got into the mindless tasks until I realised that everything looked the same. So basically, the lifespan will entirely depend on how quick you get bored of this. I got bored quite fast but I started getting really tired with the game around 10 hours but continued to get the achievements (for these count at least 60 hours). You also have to take into account that the game's time continues while you're offline (so you don't have to wait for crops while staying in the game) but also your farmhands don't do anything while offline so if you want to actually harvest stuff then you'll have to be there.

[u][b]Story :[/b][/u] No story, nothing. You have quests but they bring absolutely nothing. It's just: I need eggs, gimme gimme!

[u][b]Gameplay :[/b][/u] You basically can do 2 things: move or action. And that is already a problem, because very often I would plow the ground by mistake while trying to interact with something. Also you don't know what an action will cost so sometimes you do something and instantly regret it because you spent so much more than what you were willing to.
Your character is really slow, you get a tractor quickly enough but it barely feels faster, the only nice thing is you can interact with 9 squares at the same time, the annoying thing about it is you often have to fill it up with gas so you can use it.
Everything you do gives you experience and with this experience you can hold more gas at once and you can have a bigger boost bar. You also require a certain level to unlock every buildings/crops/animals/...
The boost bar is something you can fill up by doing tasks on other farms and it's completely useless, I never bothered. Why? Because you have to work so long on other farms to have this boost that lasts for a very short time when on your farm.
You start with a small plot of land then eventually you can expand by spending diamonds. Crops you plant have a timer before you can harvest them. This timer is real time, it can go from 10mins to 2 days! Thankfully this time will advance even when you're not playing. There are also seasons that change every 17 minutes and determine what you can plant. Since you're most likely not going to want to stay long enough to get the season you want, you'll either have to wait to randomly log on during the desired season or calculate when you need to come back.
The harvest you get contains a specific resource and money. The resource is really basic, whether you harvest a potato or a tomato it doesn't matter, you'll get "vegetable". There are 15 resources (vegetables, fruits, cereals, grapes, mushrooms, nuts, milk, eggs, fish, fabric, flowers, spice, honey, jam and cheese). You have a limited amount you can have of each and you need to build buildings to improve that. If you harvest something while full the resource will be wasted instead of not letting you harvest it or giving you a warning message or making it fall on the ground for you to pickup later. They only show you a small text that says "full" and I missed it a lot at the beginning when I didn't know what I was doing and so wasted a lot of resources.
There are 4 currencies: money, diamonds, medals and tickets. Money you get mostly from harvesting stuff and the next two you get from stands or quests. The stands are buildings you build where you can exchange resources against other things (other resources or currencies). The annoying thing is you can only exchange a very low number of resources at the same time AND you have to wait for a timer before you can exchange again. At some point you get the ability to build larger stands where you don't have to wait between exchanges but first of all they arrive far too late (you need a lot of experience to buy them) and also they give you less currency per resources! Which means when you finally get them you'll have to choose between making it much less boring but getting much less currency or taking forever to exchange everything on the small stands. With the special currencies you can buy special crops/animals and buildings. Basically the more annoying the currency, the more interesting the things you can buy with. The tickets are something you can get from doing actions in your house like playing the piano or cooking, but you're not actually doing those activities, you just get a timer as usual. You pay a currency to activate the timer and at the end you get tickets, sometimes you have to come activate the timer several times before you get your tickets (but it costs currency everytime). With those tickets you can buy decorations for your house or pay farmhands.
You can only have 15 farmhands. That seems like a lot? Compared to your huge farm it's nothing. They have a 13x13 square range (again, nothing compared to the scale of the map) and will harvest anything that's within this range. They can also feed animals which can very quickly make you broke so I would avoid if I were you. What's really disappointing is you need a lot of experience and rare currency (medals) to get them but they don't work offline, you need to be standing idly on the map for them to work.

[u][b]Achievements :[/b][/u] It took me 64 hours to finish them all and believe me I tried to make it as short as possible because I just wanted to bury that game forever. So I played as efficiently as possible and even then it took forever. There's an achievement for buying all plots of land and there are 48 plots of them you can buy!!! Not only does that require a lot of diamonds but you also need to be a certain level to be allowed to buy them which means you'll have to grind for experience and diamonds and believe me this will take forever (I bought lots of diamond trees and put farmhands in the middle of them all and would log on only when I knew they would be harvestable. While they harvested them I would fish in a gigantic lake I created to get experience). There's a lot of other grindy achievements but while you wait to get the plot one, you will definitely have gotten the others. There's an achievement for doing all quests of a special event (like christmas or whatnot) but I wouldn't worry about that, they come back regularly and you can go to other big farms to help complete them.

I really like to play this game, but at some point game itself becomes almost full time job and exhausting. The map becomes too big for players to handle either with the 3x3 tractor or farmhands. Would be cool if we can upgrade the tractor to something better than 3x3. Considering that most of the players are couples or groups of two, that would really help.

Play when you feel like it. Nothing will die if you don't play. Goals will still be there waiting. Special events have time limits, but nothing else does. It's nice if you visit other players' farms to get bonuses for yourself. It isn't required, but it does help.

In Farm Together, yes devs released a DLC (and probably more will come soon) but they also REGULARLY (not scarcely) add FREE new decorative content and harvestable items, so yes, even if you are a bit short with your money, you still have this feeling to belong to the community, and not beeing left behind as a poor man, so again here kudos for that TOO RARE behavior.

Now the game itself is... addictive, and the worst thing, it's hard to know why... I mean the game is relaxed casual gaming, nothing very complex to play it, very accessible for children, and still, as an adult, I find myself just forgetting about the time...

The first few levels can be a bit grindy, and a bit slow paced due to the "timer based" game mechanic, so early game, you may play this game in very short stints.

Notice that Devs, while putting all items under real time timer, chose the very nice approach to do it on a continouos timer, meaning that if you plant something that needs 4h to grow, you can close your game and come back 4h later and harvest it, so no need to let your game run in the background, meaning you can also play an other game from your Steam library until you come back to gather your veggies, flowers etc.

They also made a very nice decision with trees that are harvestable on a seasonal basis (some trees can be harvested every season, so 4 times a "year" and some are a one season only harvest, with everything inbetween).
Those seasons beeing 15 minutes long, if you go with a balanced farm, you'll always find something to do.

Overall, I find that game very well thought, very well balanced, with a lot of thinking behind it for what seems a very easy and simple game.

So if you are after a nice looking, easy and relax game to be played hardcore or occasionally, I can only recommand that game.

10 hours in, my first "still in early access" review.

* Quick update after 60+ hours: Game is receiving regular content updates and dev listens to player feedback. I can only recommend it more and more as a perfect little casual farm game. I will add 60+ hour comments below noted with an *

The first and most important thing you should know is, this game feels like playing a mobile game. If you don't like that, you will never like this game! <<< Really there is no way you will if those game mechanics bug you.

Now if you're still interested, this is what I found until now.

- You play on your own farm and you can visit other players farms freely. (you can own more then 1 farm/savegame)
- Default new farm settings let other people visit your farm when you're playing on it. This can easily be changed if you don't like it.
- Not playing on your own farm, then it's offline to everyone else!
- All farms are in their own world (which is HUGE), visiting others means you close your farm and load/visit theirs.
- Grieving (people trying to harm your farm): I have seen none as the default settings protect your farm, you can remove all limits if you are... uhm insane?

- You level your farm by playing on it, levels unlock more crops, animals, trees and buildings.
- You earn money by harvesting crops, trees and animals and you can earn diamonds by selling those crops.
- Diamonds are used to build buildings like your selling point shops, fuel station for your tractor and a lot of cosmetic items/buildings.
- You earn 5 diamonds per 20 crops, 10 fruits, 20 fish, 20 eggs at this moment in time.
- Doing quests give you medals which are used for special buildings like fuel stations, medals can be earned easier at a higher farm level through making special items from your farm harvests like jam, cheese and more.
- There is NO ingame shop, and NO microtransaction to buy anything.

- You also level your farmer, which unlocks cosmetics which can be freely changed anytime, again NO real money shop.
- Every day on your farm is a season, all seasons are included and crops can only be planted in the correct season (a day/season lasts 17 minutes).
- You can visit other players (A.F.A.I.K. you only see geo locations close to you, for me this is Dutch and German players)
- NO way to favorite farms or add/visit friends at this moment in time. (*THIS FEATURE HAS BEEN ADDED!)
- Everything has a visible timer which you can see and influence by watering crops and feeding animals.
- Everyone that visited me or that I visited was extremely friendly. Most just look around, some even help. (farm tourism!) (*AFTER 60+ hours a total of 1 dumb person said something stupid, it took me about 5 seconds to kick and ban him/her through easy ingame options)

The game already feels very polished, they have said that they'll add even more crops, trees and animals during early access. (*They've added plenty of new crops, animals and buildings in several patches since release)

For now after 10 hours of gameplay, this game gets a big juicy thumbs up from me as it's really fun to play.

* As said above, after 60+ hours I can only recommend this casual farm game more and more!

As a former employee of a game company, this review is based on professional experience as well as gameplay. 

Farm Together is fun, visually charming and very addictive. However, there are several things that make the gameplay much less enjoyable or rewarding than it could be. Some seriously needed improvements are:

1- The tractor should move faster than the player character does, even when the character is running.

2- The quest log should be more easily accesible with a dedicated hotkey and dedicated  pop-up window.

3- As medals are such a crucial part of the game, and quests involve many hours and resources, the number of medals you receive for completing a quest should be a minimum of 10 per quest, increasing with difficulty. 

4- Money-trees should increase the amount of diamonds you receive as they level up.

5- Seasonal quests should not be so insanely difficult, and the crops required should yield money and fruit/veggies as well as XP. 

6- When your home is built, you should also have a work-table to create the three most commonly used items: sprinklers, separators and garden lights. Sprinklers especially, as they currently cost 1 medal each.

7- No flower bed should take more than 6 hours to produce.

8- Because of how much it costs to feed them, no animal should take more than 3 hours to produce. 

9 - As the player levels up, gas pumps should also level up with more fuel.

10- Barns, water troughs, coops, greenhouses and windmills should have feeding/watering functionality, or time/resource boosts.

11- You should be able to customize colours for player clothing and accessories. You should be able to customize colours for Farm-Hand clothing as well.

12 - There should be toys and beds for your pet, and you should be able to interact with them by playing, shooing and patting. 

13- As your tractor covers 3 tiles in width, sprinklers should too. (Currently, they only cover 2 tiles.)

14- As homes have bathroom accessories, ALL houses  should have a separate room for a bathroom.

15- TVs and radios in your home currently have no fuctionality, and they should. 

16- Once they've reached the highest level, you should be able to place the easel paintings you create, on the walls in your home.

17- You should be able to select multiple road tiles for 'recycling', and selecting fencing and all edge items should be quicker and easier.

After completing this game I want to share some of my feelings about it. My "not recommended" rating comes with a reason and I'll also explain why I feel comfortable giving it, as I did enjoy the game and quite happily 100%'ed it (okay, I'm at 98%, but if you look why it makes more sense, in a week it should be 100%). 
Throughout my play-through I've found quite a few flaws and inconsistencies that I feel take away from this game's enjoyment. From what I've understood, the second game improves on a bunch of  these criticisms, so I feel fine giving a negative rating for this one and recommend people to give the second game a try as it's A LOT like the first game, but more polished and it looks like they have taken a bunch of the criticisms of this game seriously.

So let's start with the positives:
- You indeed do a lot of farming initially
- It's nice to see your farm and wealth grow
- Unlocks feel pretty good
- Playing it together is quite fun
- It's kind of cute and laid back.
- Being able to visit other people's farms is also really nice, some of the other farms are really crazy and inspirational.
- Farm customization is pretty fun, though a little limited. (they all kind of tend to look the same-ish since it's the same few handfuls of decorations, especially without the DLC's).

Then for the negatives:
- As you get further into the game, a considerable amount of your time is spent trying to sell off your produce since the selling is so slow. When you have to sell 9000 fish per 100, with an animation that takes a few seconds each, that means you are going to be spending like 5-10 minutes just sitting around with the spacebar pressed, and that is just for 1 resource.
- Income/costs of items are sort of opaque. You have no idea what sometimes might be draining your money halfway through the progression once you unlock the farm hands. Animals can cost a lot of money out of seemingly nowhere and you will be wondering while your money is close to 0. So an overview that shows the in/out for specific resources would be really nice.
- Animations are very slow. This especially becomes very obvious and annoying in the later stages of the game when you try to get some crops planted for which you only have 1 season, like chard and .
- Farmhands do not work while you are not in the game. This led me to just leaving the computer on way more than I probably should have, while letting my guy idle somewhere on the map. Personally as a developer, it seems fairly simple to simulate what they have done during your absence.
- Farmhands have zero customizability. I'd like to be able to prioritize certain tasks for example, like having them deal with plants that will not be pick-able anymore next season. They also really lack utility when it comes to normal crops. They are kind of slow and do not re-plant. To add to the previous point, it would be nice to "pause" a farmhand or tell if they should work while you are not in the game.
- Quests suck. They arguably scale negatively as they become harder and more tedious as you level and unlock stuff, while their rewards become increasingly irrelevant. Like everything you've unlocked can be asked by the quest, with many of the late game unlocks having rather long timers. It's kind of silly that a quest that has you gather 20 animal drops, 10 early game flowers and 30 of some crop with a 30-120 min timer will yield the same 30 ribbons and 3000 exp as a quest that requires you to plant 650 graffiti cauliflowers (that have a 2 day timer). 
Even for ribbons quests become completely irrelevant. There's like 4 or more other sources that are all probably faster than doing most of the quests. Jobs, gift shops and honey/candy stands all are much more effective for getting these. Quests are also quite repetitive and feel like filler content, as what you need to get for them has nothing to do with the quest.
So I think quests are quite fundamentally badly designed and there's really no reason to do them beyond a certain point.
- The "premium" resources (jam, cheese and honey) seem a bit weird, they don't really seem to mean anything and by the time you need them, you will likely just buy them using gold nuggets as that's easier to get and less time-gated than these resources themselves seem to be, as you get gold nuggets very often in the end game. Also, there seems to be little reason why they cannot have a 'fast' building to sell them at, like the other resources. Also it's strange that there's no wine resource considering there are a few grape and wine centered resource buildings.
- Storage is kinda crappy too. The late-game storage (Warehouse) offers way too little storage, with a timer that makes it very slow to level it (why does this one have a timer anyways? You get like 50 storage per upgrade and it's not like it has any sort of exponential growth effect that the boost buildings have), so everyone just ends up with filling a massive area of their map with red barns, as they are just 250 diamonds for 2x more storage than an upgrade to the warehouse (and they don't have you wait 20 minutes before you can add another 50 storage).
